_about: Care data for the Mooncat crystal care lookup. water: rinse = a quick rinse under cool water is fine (never soak, never salt or hot water); dry = keep it dry. sun: safe | fades. fragility: sturdy | careful | delicate. shop: a mooncatcrystals.com collection handle, or null to fall back to a store search. When in doubt, err on the side of caution (Kristen's rule). No scary per-stone toxicity warnings for everyday stones: a calm, universal 'good crystal habits' note covers it (not in your mouth, away from pets/kids who chew, wash hands after raw pieces). Add a 'warn' field ONLY for genuinely hazardous minerals (e.g. stibnite, crocoite, cinnabar, realgar, orpiment, galena, radioactive torbernite/autunite).

crystals.name: Amethyst
crystals.note: Its purple can fade with long sun exposure, so keep it out of sunny windows. Avoid hot water and sudden temperature changes, which can crack it.

crystals.name: Citrine
crystals.note: Citrine's color can fade with long exposure to strong sun, so keep it out of sunny windows.

crystals.name: Clear Quartz
crystals.note: Very easy to care for. One real safety note: clear quartz spheres and points can focus sunlight like a magnifying glass, so don't leave them in a sunny window near fabric, paper or wood.

crystals.name: Rose Quartz
crystals.note: Its pink fades in direct sun over time, so keep it away from sunny windows. Many pieces have natural internal fractures, so avoid drops and sudden temperature changes.

crystals.name: Smoky Quartz
crystals.note: Strong sun and heat can lighten its color over time. Otherwise it's an easy, durable stone.

crystals.name: Herkimer Diamond
crystals.note: Hard like all quartz, but the small, sharp double points can chip if they knock against other stones. Store it on its own or in a soft pouch.

crystals.name: Rutilated Quartz
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Dry it right after a rinse.

crystals.name: Tourmalinated Quartz
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Dry it right after a rinse.

crystals.name: Tiger's Eye
crystals.note: A quick rinse is fine. Dry it right away so water doesn't sit in its fibers.

crystals.name: Carnelian
crystals.note: Durable and easy to keep. Some carnelian on the market is dyed; if yours is an unusually bright, even orange, keep it out of water and strong sun to be safe.

crystals.name: Green Aventurine
crystals.note: A quick rinse is fine. Its color can fade with long sun exposure, so keep it out of sunny windows.

crystals.name: Agate
crystals.note: Natural agate is fine with a quick rinse. Many brightly colored agates (hot pink, teal, purple slices) are dyed, and water or strong sun can make the dye fade or bleed. If yours is a color that doesn't occur in nature, keep it dry and out of the sun.

crystals.name: Blue Lace Agate
crystals.note: A quick rinse is fine. Its soft blue can fade in strong sun over time, so keep it out of sunny windows.

crystals.name: Moss Agate
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Dry it right after a rinse.

crystals.name: Red Jasper
crystals.note: A quick rinse is fine. Dry it right away, and skip soaking.

crystals.name: Dragon's Blood Jasper
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Dry it right after a rinse.

crystals.name: Mookaite
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Dry it right after a rinse.

crystals.name: Bloodstone
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Dry it right after a rinse.

crystals.name: Black Onyx
crystals.note: Most black onyx is dyed chalcedony with a very stable color. A quick rinse is fine; skip soaking.

crystals.name: Petrified Wood
crystals.note: Wood that has turned to stone (mostly quartz). A quick rinse is fine. Pieces with visible cracks or bark-like edges can flake, so handle those gently.

crystals.name: Ohio Flint
crystals.note: Hard and durable. Raw pieces can have sharp edges.

crystals.name: Selenite
crystals.note: Keep Selenite completely dry. Water dissolves and damages it, so never rinse or soak it; dust it with a soft, dry cloth. It's soft enough to scratch with a fingernail, so handle it gently.

crystals.name: Black Tourmaline
crystals.note: More delicate than it looks. It can split and shed splinters along its lines, especially raw pieces, so handle it gently and keep it where it won't get knocked around.

crystals.name: Obsidian
crystals.note: Obsidian is volcanic glass, so it can chip or shatter if dropped, and raw pieces can have edges sharp enough to cut. Handle raw pieces carefully.

crystals.name: Fluorite
crystals.note: Soft and splits easily along flat planes, so a drop can chip or cleave it. Its colors can fade in sunlight, so keep it out of sunny windows.

crystals.name: Labradorite
crystals.note: Scratches dull its flash, so store it away from harder stones and wipe it with a soft cloth.

crystals.name: Moonstone
crystals.note: Moonstone can crack along internal planes if knocked, and scratches easily against harder stones. Store it on its own or in a soft pouch.

crystals.name: Pyrite
crystals.note: Keep Pyrite dry. Water and humidity can make it rust or tarnish, so don't keep it in a bathroom. It's brittle and can crack if dropped.

crystals.name: Hematite
crystals.note: Hematite is iron-rich and can rust if it stays damp. It's also brittle and can crack or shatter if dropped on a hard floor.

crystals.name: Malachite
crystals.note: Soft and scratches easily. Keep it dry and away from household cleaners.

crystals.name: Celestite
crystals.note: Its soft blue fades in sunlight, and the crystals in a cluster are soft and break easily. Keep it out of the sun, dust it with a soft brush, and don't pick clusters up by the points.

crystals.name: Lepidolite
crystals.note: Lepidolite is a soft, layered mica, so raw pieces can flake. Polished pieces are sturdier but still scratch easily.

crystals.name: Howlite
crystals.note: Soft and porous, so it can absorb water, oils and lotions. Howlite is also often dyed to look like turquoise; dyed pieces can bleed color if they get wet.

crystals.name: Sodalite
crystals.note: Moderately soft, so store it away from harder stones to avoid scratches.

crystals.name: Lapis Lazuli
crystals.note: Lapis is fairly soft and often contains flecks of pyrite, which can tarnish if wet. Keep it dry and away from harder stones.

crystals.name: Amazonite
crystals.note: Amazonite can split along flat planes if knocked, and its color can fade with long sun exposure.

crystals.name: Rhodonite
crystals.note: Moderately hard, but the black veins can be softer. Store it away from harder stones.

crystals.name: Rhodochrosite
crystals.note: Soft, easily scratched and sensitive to heat. Keep it out of the sun and away from household cleaners.

crystals.name: Kunzite
crystals.note: Kunzite's pink fades in sunlight (it's sometimes called the evening stone), and it can split cleanly if knocked. Keep it out of the sun and handle it gently.

crystals.name: Morganite
crystals.note: Hard and durable. To protect its soft pink, keep it out of strong, direct sun.

crystals.name: Aquamarine
crystals.note: Hard and durable. Some aquamarine has been heat-treated for color, so keep it out of strong, direct sun to be safe.

crystals.name: Garnet
crystals.note: Durable and easy to care for. Raw pieces in matrix can crumble, so handle those gently.

crystals.name: Jade
crystals.note: Jade is very tough, but much of it is waxed, polished or dyed. Wipe it with a soft cloth rather than getting it wet.

crystals.name: Chrysocolla
crystals.note: Soft and can dry out and crack in heat or strong sun. Keep it cool, dry and out of the sun.

crystals.name: Turquoise
crystals.note: Turquoise is porous: it can absorb water, oils and lotions and change color, and strong sun can dry it out. Many pieces are stabilized or dyed.

crystals.name: Opal
crystals.note: Opal holds water inside it, and heat, strong sun or very dry air can make it crack (called crazing). Keep it out of the sun and away from heat sources. Some opals soak up water and change appearance, so keep them dry.

crystals.name: Amber
crystals.note: Amber is fossilized tree resin, not a stone: very soft, sensitive to heat, and sunlight can darken it and make it brittle. Keep it away from perfume, hairspray and cleaners.

crystals.name: Sunstone
crystals.note: Can crack along internal planes if knocked, and scratches against harder stones. Store it on its own.

crystals.name: Calcite
crystals.note: Calcite is soft, splits easily, and is damaged by anything acidic, even lemon or vinegar. Some colors fade in sun. Keep it dry and out of sunny windows.

crystals.name: Aragonite
crystals.note: Soft and brittle; star clusters break easily. Keep it dry and out of strong sun.

crystals.name: Apophyllite
crystals.note: The crystals can flake or chip, especially at the points. Dust clusters with a soft brush and don't pick them up by the points.

crystals.name: Shungite
crystals.note: Shungite can leave black dust on your hands and surfaces. Keep it dry.

crystals.name: Prophecy Stone
crystals.note: Prophecy stones are iron-rich and can rust or shed rusty dust if they get damp. Keep them dry.

crystals.name: Moqui Marbles
crystals.note: Iron-rich sandstone balls. They can rust or crumble if they stay wet, so keep them dry and handle them gently.
